- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward to reflect market resilience or reversal.
- Model often overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5+ points) by forecasting further gains; cap or dampen subsequent peaks.
- Forecast mean reversion bias: if 3-5 consecutive days show downward trend, model may lag in correcting; add slight upward bias to counteract lag.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently misses late-period momentum; anchor forecast toward last 5-7 days of history for final 10-15 days.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; trigger early correction if sentiment > 0.5 after day 10.
- Avoid forecasting below 60% of recent 10-day average unless sentiment strongly negative; use sentiment as a floor/ceiling filter.
